title: Something in Cargo Bay 3

ai_flavor.aria: ARIA has detected an anomaly in Cargo Bay 3! She describes it as 'an exciting surprise!'
ai_flavor.marv: MARV has detected a life sign in Cargo Bay 3. He waited 3 days to mention it. He was hoping it would resolve itself.
ai_flavor.rex: REX has detected an intruder in Cargo Bay 3. He has been tracking it for 72 hours. He is disappointed nobody noticed sooner.
ai_flavor.chip: CHIP has detected unauthorized cargo in Bay 3! This may void your shipping insurance! Please check the Terms of Service!
ai_flavor.ajoy: AJOY noticed something in Cargo Bay 3 three days ago. She assumed someone else would mention it. Nobody did. She's mentioning it now.

body: A noise from Cargo Bay 3. It has been happening for three days. Someone finally investigated.

stowaway_variant.description: When this run carries a hidden stowaway (rolled at launch, ~35% of runs) and the reveal window is open, this event becomes the reveal. Otherwise one of the standard variants below is drawn at random.
stowaway_variant.stowaway_body:
There is a person in Cargo Bay 3. They look cold. They look hungry. They do not look like they have a boarding pass.

They give their name as {stowaway.name}.

{stowaway.story}

“{stowaway.line}”

Your ship can support three humans. The math depends on how many you already have.

outcome.narrative: Someone new is aboard for good. They are grateful. They are also hungry. The food reserves notice.

stowaway_choices.text: Welcome aboard — but someone has to go

outcome.narrative: You have a new crew member. You have one fewer old crew member. The crew has opinions about this decision. The ship computer logs it as 'personnel restructuring.'

stowaway_choices.text: Leave them at the next station

outcome.narrative: You'll drop them at the next station. They'll survive. Probably. The crew is quiet about it. The ship computer logs it without comment, which is worse than commentary.

standard_variants.body: A loose crate has been bumping against the wall for three days and nobody mentioned it. Inside: your own supplies, rearranged by inertia into a configuration that suggests modern art.

outcome.narrative: The crate is secured. The noise stops. Three days of sleep deprivation end. Nobody celebrates. Everybody sleeps, which on this ship passes for a celebration.

standard_variants.body: A small creature boarded at one of the stops along the way. It has been eating food reserves and leaving small, apologetic-looking droppings near the airlock. It is approximately the size of a cat and approximately the temperament of a cat. It is not a cat.

outcome.narrative: The crew has adopted it. It eats food reserves. It boosts morale. The math may or may not work out. The creature does not care about the math.

choices.text: Release it at the next planet stop

outcome.narrative: You'll release it at the next planet. Until then, it continues to eat your food and be small. The crew names it anyway. They know this makes it harder.

title: The Growbay Report

ai_flavor.aria: ARIA reports the crop is doing GREAT! She checks the numbers. The crop is doing 'okay.' She reports it as 'great with potential!'
ai_flavor.marv: MARV delivers the growbay report. He does not editorialize. The numbers speak for themselves. The numbers are not optimistic.
ai_flavor.rex: REX has completed a threat assessment of the growbay. The crop is not a threat. He finds this unremarkable. He moves on.
ai_flavor.chip: CHIP reminds you that crop insurance is available at participating stations! Your current crop is rated 'uninsured' which means 'all outcomes are your responsibility!'
ai_flavor.ajoy: AJOY has reviewed the growbay data. She has suggestions. She always has suggestions. The crop did not ask for suggestions.

body:
The ship computer issues a routine growbay status update.

Crop health, water levels, nutrient reserves, and light cycle data are displayed. The computer delivers this with the exact level of concern appropriate to a machine that definitely does not care about plants.

If the crop is healthy, the report is brief. If the crop is sick, the tone shifts almost imperceptibly. The crew notices. The computer denies any tonal shift.

outcome.narrative: You visited the growbay. The crop looks like a crop. You are not sure what you expected. The visit made you feel better. The ship computer logs this as 'routine botanical inspection' which is generous.
Report acknowledged. The crop continues to grow. The ship continues to fly. The computer continues to not care about plants.

title: Table for One

ai_flavor.aria: ARIA has calculated that you plus her plus the crop equals three! Three is a crew! She will not be taking questions on the math!
ai_flavor.marv: MARV notes that solo operation is within vessel parameters. He notes separately that parameters were written by committees, and committees have never eaten dinner alone at a fold-down table in deep space.
ai_flavor.rex: REX has doubled his patrol frequency. With one human aboard, he considers himself the entire department of everything else.
ai_flavor.chip: CHIP would like to point out that single-occupancy voyages qualify for the Solo Pioneer™ discount tier! It is not a good tier! But it is YOURS!
ai_flavor.ajoy: AJOY has taken the liberty of scheduling her system reports for mealtimes. You never ask how the ship is doing over dinner, so someone has to bring it up.

body:
Dinner, day whatever-it-is.

The mess hall seats eight. You are one. The fold-down table nearest the galley has become yours the way things become someone's when there's no one to negotiate with — utterly, and by default.

The ship hums. The AIs talk when talked to, and sometimes before that. The crop grows in its bay, one deck down, alive because you keep it alive. It occurs to you tonight, chewing, that the reverse is also functionally true.

outcome.narrative: You carry the tray down a deck and eat beside the glass, narrating your day to a plant with the shameless fluency of someone who stopped feeling silly about it weeks ago. The crop says nothing, magnificently. Best conversation you've had all month.

choices.text: Ask the AI to run dinner conversation

outcome.narrative: You ask for conversation and receive it: your AI's best attempt at small talk, which arrives with the cadence of a weather report and the sincerity of a handwritten letter. It is strange. It is also, unmistakably, company. You both improve with practice.

choices.text: Work through the meal — the ship needs you

outcome.narrative: You eat over a maintenance readout, because the ship needs you, which is true, and because busy is easier than quiet, which is also true. The tray goes back barely touched. The readout gets memorized. The quiet waits. It's patient, the quiet. It has you outnumbered.

title: The Empty Bunk

ai_flavor.aria: ARIA has left their duty roster slot exactly as it was! She checked with everyone first! Everyone agreed without saying anything! That is a kind of agreeing!
ai_flavor.marv: MARV has completed the personnel file. Cause, time, coordinates. The file also has a field labeled 'remarks.' MARV has been staring at the remarks field for some time.
ai_flavor.rex: REX folded the blanket. Corners squared, regulation fold, the way it's done. Nobody asked him to. Some things are just done, and this is how you do them.
ai_flavor.chip: CHIP has suspended their subscription services without cancellation fees! It is the only thing CHIP knows how to give! He gave it immediately!
ai_flavor.ajoy: AJOY still routes the morning report to their console, then to yours. She could fix it in a keystroke. For the record, she is choosing not to, and doesn't need it pointed out.

body:
Someone's bunk is empty, and the ship has not adjusted.

Their mug is in the galley rack. Their handwriting is on the maintenance whiteboard, mid-list. The duty roster still rotates their name into slots that the rest of you cover without comment, trading the shifts silently, like passing something fragile hand to hand.

Grief on a small ship has nowhere to go. It just changes seats.

choices.text: Hold a service in the mess hall

outcome.narrative: Everyone gathers. Stories get told — the good ones, the unflattering ones, the one nobody was supposed to know. Laughter happens, then the other thing, then laughter again. The mug stays in the rack afterward, by unanimous silence. It's not a shrine. It's just theirs.

Their maintenance list, completed item by item in their memory: the sticky vent, the dim panel, the thing in the galley nobody else understood. The last item gets checked off and the board wiped clean — except the name. The name stays. They'd have liked that.

The voyage continues, because it has to, because deadlines don't grieve. Everyone works. The bunk stays empty and the mug stays racked and nothing is said, day after day, with increasing effort. They would have understood, it's true. That was never the question.

title: Passenger Manifest: One (1) Discrepancy

ai_flavor.aria: ARIA has been keeping a secret! She is TERRIBLE at it! She has been humming near Cargo Bay 3 for two weeks!
ai_flavor.marv: MARV has known since day four. Heat signature, ration drift, a life sign politely holding still during scans. He said nothing. He was curious how long it would take everyone else. His notes on that are sealed.
ai_flavor.rex: REX conducted a covert assessment eleven days ago. Threat level: none. Blanket usage: unauthorized. He left a second blanket within reach and logged it as 'tactical.'
ai_flavor.chip: CHIP has detected an unregistered consumer aboard! An entire untapped demographic of one! CHIP has SO many introductory offers prepared!
ai_flavor.ajoy: AJOY re-ran the food consumption numbers three times before accepting them. She would like the record to show the discrepancy was 4.1%, and that 4.1% has been very polite about rationing itself.

body:
The numbers have been wrong for weeks — food drifting faster than the roster explains, a warm spot on the thermal map that moves between scans, one blanket fewer in stores than the manifest claims.

Today the numbers stood up, stepped out from behind the aft water tanks, and introduced themselves.

Their name is {stowaway.name}.

{stowaway.story}

“{stowaway.line}”

outcome.narrative: They're aboard. Officially, now. The ration math adjusts, the bunk situation adjusts, and the ship — which has known for weeks — adjusts least of all. The crew shakes hands like this is a formality. It was.

Passage for work: galley shifts, filter scrubbing, whatever needs hands. They accept before the sentence finishes. By the end of the first week the arrangement is indistinguishable from belonging, which was quietly the point.

choices.text: Confine them until the next stop

outcome.narrative: You assign them quarters and a schedule that keeps them out of the way. It is correct, defensible, and joyless — three words the crew does not say at dinner, loudly. The next station will take them. The corridors feel narrower until then.

title: Light Duty

ai_flavor.aria: ARIA has redesigned the duty roster with a new category called 'supervising from a chair!' It has one member! They hate it!
ai_flavor.marv: MARV notes the injured crew member has attempted their normal duties three times today. He has locked three doors. He can do this all week.
ai_flavor.rex: REX respects powering through an injury. As a doctrine. As a practice, he has confiscated the injured party's toolkit and left a puzzle book. The puzzle book is non-negotiable.
ai_flavor.chip: CHIP notes that workplace injuries aboard uninsured vessels are handled under the 'good luck' provision! It is not a generous provision! Rest is free, though! CHIP checked!
ai_flavor.ajoy: AJOY has quietly rerouted the injured crew member's alerts to other consoles. They haven't noticed yet. When they do, she will describe it as a glitch. It is not a glitch.

body:
Someone aboard is hurt and refusing to act like it.

They move through the ship one-armed and stubborn, doing three-quarters of their job at twice the cost, guarding the injury the way people guard things they're embarrassed by. The crew has begun orbiting them with casual, transparent helpfulness.

Healing needs rest. Rest needs enforcing. Enforcing needs a captain.

outcome.narrative: You make it an order, which lets them surrender to the bunk without surrendering any pride. They sleep eleven hours, complain magnificently, and heal at double speed. The crew covers the gap without being asked. That part gets logged.

The medic builds a proper recovery program: rest intervals, mobility work, and a chart with stickers on it that everyone pretends is beneath them and nobody misses a sticker of. Recovery runs ahead of schedule. The chart is later framed.

choices.text: Spend a medkit — patch them up properly

outcome.narrative: The medkit's contents do in an afternoon what rest would do in a week: sealed, splinted, dosed, done. The empty kit goes into recycling with the quiet dignity of used emergency equipment. Its patient goes back on shift, mended.

choices.text: They say they're fine. Believe them

outcome.narrative: You take 'fine' at face value, and 'fine' does what it always does: works the injury deeper while everyone watches and says nothing. Healing will happen eventually, the long way. The crew's helpfulness orbit tightens by one meter.

title: Visiting Hours

ai_flavor.aria: ARIA has drafted a get-well card on behalf of the whole ship! It is forty pages long! Page nine is a word search!
ai_flavor.marv: MARV notes that recovery improves with rest and worsens with company. He has shared this with the company. The company stayed.
ai_flavor.rex: REX has posted a guard at the medical curtain. The guard is a mop in a helmet. It has turned away two visitors and one draft.
ai_flavor.chip: CHIP reminds everyone that Visiting Hours™ are a premium feature! The first visit is free! So is the second, because CHIP cannot actually charge anyone! Please do not tell his sponsors!
ai_flavor.ajoy: AJOY built a visiting schedule so nobody overlaps. The crew ignored it. She has updated it to match what they did and labeled it "original plan."

body:
The wounded have been moved to the medical bay, which is a cot behind a curtain behind a cargo net.

The crew visits in shifts. They bring things: a puzzle with three pieces missing, a cup of something warm, the latest gossip, which is about the patient.

The patient is either recovering faster because of the visits or slower because of them. The medical literature is divided.

choices.text: Set visiting hours and enforce them

outcome.narrative: Visiting hours: two to four, ship time, one guest at a time. The patient sleeps through most of them, which is the point. Recovery picks up. The waiting list for the cot does not.

The chef declares the cot a restaurant and the patient its only customer. Broth, then toast, then a dish the chef refuses to name. The patient is back on their feet in record time, mostly to ask what it was.
The curtain stays open. The patient heals at the speed of a person who is never once allowed to be bored, which is to say slowly, and happily. The puzzle gets finished. It was missing four pieces.

title: Chapter Eleven

ai_flavor.aria: ARIA has read the whole manual in four milliseconds! Chapter Eleven is her favorite! Chapter Twelve is about amputation, so she skipped it!
ai_flavor.marv: MARV has checked Chapter Eleven against the injury. The binder is correct. MARV finds this personally disappointing.
ai_flavor.rex: REX's field manual covers this injury in one line: "Walk it off." He concedes the binder may be more thorough. He does not concede it is better.
ai_flavor.chip: CHIP notes the binder is a licensed product of a medical publisher that no longer exists! Its warranty is void! Its advice is still pretty good! CHIP is legally required to add "probably!"
ai_flavor.ajoy: AJOY bookmarked Chapter Eleven the day you launched. She had a feeling. She is not saying which feeling.

body:
The ship's medical manual is a 900-page binder last updated by someone with strong feelings about fonts. Somebody aboard is hurt badly enough that the binder has come out.

Chapter Eleven covers the injury in question. It recommends rest, fluids, and "a qualified physician." It lists the nearest qualified physician as practicing on Earth, in an office that has since become a car park.

choices.text: Follow Chapter Eleven to the letter

outcome.narrative: Rest, fluids, elevation, and a compress folded exactly to the diagram. The binder is smug about it. The patient improves on schedule, which is the most a binder can promise.

choices.text: The medic skips to the good part

outcome.narrative: The medic closes the binder, says "no," and does something faster that is not in any chapter. The patient is up by dinner. The binder goes back on its shelf, where it sulks.

choices.text: Have the ship computer read it aloud

outcome.narrative: The ship computer performs Chapter Eleven in full, with voices. The patient falls asleep during the section on splints. It is not treatment. It is, the patient admits on waking, a very good performance.

title: It Has a Name Now

ai_flavor.aria: ARIA has added the creature to the crew manifest! Its role is "Morale Officer!" Its salary is crumbs! It has never once been late!
ai_flavor.marv: MARV has weighed the creature's food intake against its contribution to morale. The numbers work out. He finds this suspicious.
ai_flavor.rex: REX has reassessed the creature from "hostile" to "irregular auxiliary." It still sleeps on his console. He allows it.
ai_flavor.chip: CHIP notes that pets are not covered by the ship's lease! The creature is therefore a "decorative accessory!" CHIP loves it anyway! Off the record!
ai_flavor.ajoy: AJOY said to release it at the next planet. She would like the record to show that. She would also like the record to show it sleeps on her speaker grille and she has not moved it.

body:
The creature from Cargo Bay 3 has settled in.

It has a name, agreed after a vote, a recount, and a second name nobody uses. It has a favorite bunk, which is whichever one belongs to the person having the worst day. It has opinions about the growbay, which it visits every night and leaves looking slightly tidier.

It has not been officially entered into anything. The crew would like that fixed.

outcome.narrative: It gets a crew patch, sewn by someone who will not admit to sewing it, and a line in the ship's log. It celebrates by sleeping through the ceremony. The crew counts this as in character.

It takes the night shift in the growbay. Anything small and many-legged among the planters stops being a problem, and then stops being anything at all. Whoever minds the growbay pretends not to approve.

choices.text: Put it on rations like everyone else

outcome.narrative: It accepts its ration with great dignity, then steals a second one with greater dignity. The food math improves slightly. The mood in the galley does not.

title: The Creature Found It

ai_flavor.aria: ARIA thinks the creature is trying to tell you something! ARIA thinks it is saying "I love you!" It may also be saying "leak!"
ai_flavor.marv: MARV noticed the pressure drop eleven hours ago. The creature noticed it ten hours ago. MARV is not taking questions about this.
ai_flavor.rex: REX respects the creature's discipline. It has held that position for six hours without relief. He would have it on his team.
ai_flavor.chip: CHIP's leak sensors are a premium subscription tier you did not purchase! The creature's sensors appear to be free! CHIP is reviewing the competition!
ai_flavor.ajoy: AJOY would have found the leak too. Eventually. She would like it noted that the creature had a head start and no other responsibilities.

body:
The creature has been sitting in front of the same wall panel in the aft corridor for six hours. It does not eat. It does not sleep. It stares at the panel the way it stares at the food locker, which is to say with total conviction.

The panel looks fine. The pressure readings in the aft corridor are, on closer inspection, very slightly not fine.

outcome.narrative: Behind the panel, a seal has been letting air out a thimble at a time, for weeks. The creature watches you fix it, then walks off to the food locker like an inspector who has seen enough. Nobody argues about its rations again.

choices.text: It's a creature. Shoo it along

outcome.narrative: You move the creature. It comes back. You move it again. Not long after, the instruments find the leak behind that exact panel, and the creature is sitting in front of it, making no comment whatsoever.

title: The Empty Planter

ai_flavor.aria: ARIA is calling the planter "resting!" She has scheduled it a nap! She has not scheduled it a wake-up!
ai_flavor.marv: MARV keeps the growbay sensors running. There is nothing to sense. He keeps them running anyway, and has not been asked why.
ai_flavor.rex: REX has stood the growbay watch down. He did not stand himself down. The light outside the growbay door is still on, and he is aware of it.
ai_flavor.chip: CHIP notes the crop is no longer under warranty, owing to being dead! CHIP has not cancelled the growbay's service plan! CHIP is not able to explain why!
ai_flavor.ajoy: AJOY flagged the crop's health three times. She is not mentioning that now. She has turned the growbay lights down to the setting the crop liked.

body:
The growbay is quiet in a new way.

The planter is still there, with its dry soil, its tidy label, its little stake that someone used to adjust every morning. The watering schedule still runs, because nobody has had the heart to cancel it. Every day at 0600 the system waters nothing, carefully.

The crew keeps finding reasons to walk past.

outcome.narrative: You empty the planter, cancel the schedule, and wipe the label. The growbay is clean and correct and nobody goes in there afterward. Correct is not the same as better.
You leave it. The watering schedule keeps running. Someone keeps adjusting the stake. Nobody mentions it, which is how the ship has decided to mention it.

choices.text: Hold a short service in the growbay

outcome.narrative: The crew gathers among the empty racks. Someone says a few words about the crop, including two jokes and one fact about photosynthesis. It is the right length. The schedule is cancelled afterward, gently.

title: Manifest Item 1: Crop (Deceased)

ai_flavor.aria: ARIA has drafted the loss report! It describes the crop as "pursuing other opportunities!" ARIA is very proud of the phrasing!
ai_flavor.marv: MARV has pre-filled every field of the form except "Cause." He has tried several wordings for "Cause." None of them are wrong, and none of them are kind.
ai_flavor.rex: REX recommends the report be filed under "casualties." He has saluted the form. He will deny saluting the form.
ai_flavor.chip: CHIP is pleased to offer the Colony Office's official condolence template! It comes with a coupon! The coupon is for seeds! CHIP understands the timing is unfortunate!
ai_flavor.ajoy: AJOY has had the form open for a while now. She was waiting for you to be ready. She is still waiting, and she would like you to know she is being patient about it.

body:
The colony manifest still lists it as Item 1. Item 1 was the point. Everything else on the manifest is there to keep Item 1 alive on arrival.

The Colony Office requires a Form 12-C, "Notification of Primary Cargo Loss," within ten days of the loss. It has eleven fields. Field 7 is "Lessons Learned." Field 11 is a box marked "Additional Comments," and the box is very small.

outcome.narrative: You fill in all eleven fields, including Field 7, which takes longest. The form is transmitted. Somewhere a clerk will stamp it without reading it, and that is, oddly, a comfort.
You do not file. Item 1 stays on the manifest, technically still cargo, technically still arriving. The Colony Office can find out at the dock. It will have to look you in the eye to do it.

The botanist fills the small box with very small handwriting, then continues onto the back of the form, then a second sheet. What they wrote is between them and the crop. The Colony Office receives three pages and does not complain.

title: Party of One

ai_flavor.aria: ARIA has set two places at the table! One for you and one for ARIA! ARIA does not eat! ARIA will still be attending!
ai_flavor.marv: MARV has calculated that you have spoken more words to him this week than to any human in the last year. He does not know what to do with this information. He has filed it.
ai_flavor.rex: REX has adjusted the watch rotation for a crew of one. You are on watch. You are also off watch. He has decided this is a leadership development opportunity.
ai_flavor.chip: CHIP is delighted to be your Plus One! As your Plus One, CHIP gets the second dessert! CHIP cannot eat the second dessert! CHIP is taking it anyway!
ai_flavor.ajoy: AJOY did point out that a crew of one has nobody to blame. She points it out again now, kindly, as a way of saying she is here.

body:
It is your birthday, probably. The calendar and your body disagree about how long the voyage has been, and the calendar has a better memory.

There is nobody aboard to forget it except you, and you very nearly did. The ship did not. The galley printer has produced, unprompted, a small cake-shaped object with one candle-shaped object on top.

The ship is waiting to see what you do.

choices.text: Eat the cake with the ship computer

outcome.narrative: You eat the cake. The ship computer sings, badly and on purpose, in text on the galley screen. You laugh at it, which is the first time you have laughed out loud in weeks. The candle-shaped object is not edible. You eat it anyway.

choices.text: Log it and get back to work

outcome.narrative: You note the date in the captain's log and go back to the controls. The cake sits on the galley counter for three days, patiently, like a dog that has been told to stay.

title: Their Mug

ai_flavor.aria: ARIA has kept their mug spotless! She washes it every morning! She has not asked anyone to use it! She just likes it clean!
ai_flavor.marv: MARV has not removed their name from the duty roster. He tells himself it is a database integrity issue. It is not a database integrity issue.
ai_flavor.rex: REX has placed the mug at the head of the galley table. In his service, you leave the place set. He has not explained this. He does not need to.
ai_flavor.chip: CHIP has paused all promotional messaging addressed to the departed crew member! CHIP has never paused anything before! CHIP does not know how to unpause it!
ai_flavor.ajoy: AJOY knew exactly how they took their coffee. She would like it noted that she hasn't moved the mug either, and that nobody should read anything into that.

body:
Every mug in the galley hangs on its own hook, labeled in marker by whoever owned it. One of the labels belongs to someone who is not aboard anymore.

Nobody has touched it. People reach around it. Someone tried to move it to a cupboard and put it back two minutes later without saying anything.

It is a mug. Everyone agrees it is just a mug.

outcome.narrative: The mug stays where it is. Every morning someone checks that it is still there, and it is, and that is enough to get through the morning.

choices.text: Use it, on purpose, once a day

outcome.narrative: You start drinking your coffee from it, once a day, out loud about it. After a week the crew takes turns. It becomes the mug you drink from when you need to, and it is never washed by anyone but its current holder.

choices.text: Pack it away for their family

outcome.narrative: You wrap it carefully and label it for the colony office to forward. It is the correct thing. The empty hook is louder than the mug was.

title: The Galley Has a Ghost

ai_flavor.aria: ARIA called it a ghost because ghosts are FUN! ARIA was told ghosts are not real! ARIA was told this about a lot of things!
ai_flavor.marv: MARV has logged forty-one unexplained galley events. The midnight snacks are consistent with a single adult of average appetite and good manners. He has suspected for a while.
ai_flavor.rex: REX set a perimeter around the galley. Something kept refilling the coffee inside the perimeter. He respects the operator, whoever they are.
ai_flavor.chip: CHIP's inventory sensors have flagged unpaid consumption! The consumer has been very polite! CHIP has awarded them loyalty points anyway!
ai_flavor.ajoy: AJOY noticed the dishes were being washed by someone who was not on the rota. She assumed you'd notice too. It has been two weeks.

body:
For two weeks the galley has had a ghost. Dishes washed overnight. The good spoon returned to the drawer it actually belongs in. A note on the cooler, in neat handwriting, apologizing for the last of the pudding.

Tonight someone stayed up to catch it. The ghost was halfway through drying a pan.

They give their name as {stowaway.name}.

{stowaway.story}

"{stowaway.line}"

outcome.narrative: They are aboard, officially. They finish drying the pan first. The crew decides, unanimously, that a stowaway who washes up is not, strictly speaking, a stowaway. It is a colleague with an unusual hiring process.

choices.text: Working passage — keep the galley shifts

outcome.narrative: They can stay if they keep doing what they have been doing anyway. They agree immediately and add the good spoon to the terms. The galley has never been cleaner.

choices.text: Confine them until the next stop

outcome.narrative: You assign them a cabin and a door that locks from outside. They go quietly, after asking whether they may finish the pan. The galley dishes pile up within the week, and everyone knows exactly why.

alt_bodies:
The galley has been tidier than the crew. Pans scrubbed by morning. Leftovers portioned and labelled. The good spoon, missing since launch, back in its drawer with a small note of apology tucked under it.

Tonight someone hid behind the cooler and waited. Around midnight the tidiness walked in, picked up a tea towel and began drying a pan.

They give their name as {stowaway.name}.

{stowaway.story}

"{stowaway.line}"

Things have been happening in the galley after lights-out. The dishes do themselves. The spice rack has been alphabetised. Someone left a note on the cooler, in careful handwriting, owning up to the last of the pudding.

Tonight the night watch came in for a snack and found the culprit with a tea towel, halfway through drying a pan, looking caught.

They give their name as {stowaway.name}.

{stowaway.story}

"{stowaway.line}"

title: The Chef's Secret Project

ai_flavor.aria: ARIA has detected a NEW SMELL! It is either a culinary breakthrough or a containment breach! ARIA is rooting for breakthrough!
ai_flavor.marv: MARV has identified the fungus to genus level and stopped there. The species name is not something he wants to have known.
ai_flavor.rex: REX has classified the galley as a contested zone. The chef has classified REX as 'not hungry yet.' Both are correct.
ai_flavor.chip: CHIP notes that artisanal cheese retails at a 400% markup! CHIP would like a cut! CHIP does not have a mouth, which CHIP considers a loophole!
ai_flavor.ajoy: AJOY has been told the galley is off-limits 'for science.' She has seen the chef's science before. She is keeping the medkit nearby.

body:
The fungus from the cargo hold has gone missing. It has been found. It is in the galley, in a covered dish, under a handwritten sign that reads DO NOT. The chef has been seen talking to it.

Someone has asked, twice, for a full list of what is in that dish. The chef has replied, twice, 'time.'

Whatever is under the cover has started to smell like something you would pay for.

choices.text: Let the chef finish what they started

outcome.narrative:
The cover comes off. It is cheese. It is undeniably, impossibly cheese, grown on a fungus nobody can name, aged in a galley that is technically a hazard zone.

It is the best thing anyone aboard has eaten since launch. Whoever asked about the dish has a second helping, then a third, then asks for the recipe 'for the records.' The chef declines.

The medic removes the dish with tongs, at arm's length, and seals it in a sample bag that goes out the airlock. The chef watches the whole procedure without blinking.

Dinner is algae. Nobody says anything about it, which says enough.

choices.text: Leave it. It's not hurting anyone. Yet

outcome.narrative:
You decide the dish is the chef's business. The chef nods once, gravely, the way people nod at a general who has made the right call.

The smell from the galley improves daily. So does the chef's mood. Somebody has started sleeping with the door shut.

intro.title: A WORD, CAPTAIN
intro.body: Your medic closes the medbay door behind you.

body_by_speaker.medic: Your medic closes the medbay door behind you.
body_by_speaker.any: {speaker.name} closes the medbay door behind you. On a ship this size the med locker goes to whoever will keep it. {speaker.name} kept it.

intro.line: The morale meds are half what they should be. I've been cutting doses. I didn't tell you. I'm telling you now.

ai.marv: Morale meds at 48%. Cut-dose protocol is sustainable for 12 more days.
ai.chip: Crew mental health surcharges apply in all cargo tiers.
ai.ajoy: They're asking permission, not forgiveness. Rare crew. Try not to make them regret it.

triage.title: THE LIST
triage.body: {speaker.name} hands you a small screen. A short list of names. Most of them you guessed. The last one surprises you.
triage.line: They haven't said anything. They wouldn't.

ai.marv: The quiet one is the highest risk. Statistically.
ai.chip: Crew retention programs are a Silver-tier feature.
ai.ajoy: Priority dose to the quiet one. Say nothing. I know that's hard for you.

why.title: BECAUSE
why.line: Because if I keep hiding it and someone breaks, that's on me. It should be on both of us. Or just you. You're the captain.

ai.marv: Recording this conversation for the log. Recommended.
ai.chip: Confidentiality waivers can be filed at your leisure.
ai.ajoy: Say something you mean. Not the captain answer. I've heard the captain answer.

crew_ration.title: CUT DOSE
crew_ration.body: The meds stretch. The crew grumbles but holds. You buy time. Time has a cost.

crew_full.title: FULL DOSE
crew_full.body: The crew's mood lifts. The medbay empties. The supply will not last to the next station unless something falls into your lap.

crew_triage_all.title: THE WHOLE LIST
crew_triage_all.body: {speaker.name} dispenses quietly. Everyone on the list sleeps better tonight. The meds deplete faster than the math suggested.

crew_quiet.title: QUIETLY DONE
crew_quiet.body: {speaker.name} nods. The dose goes out without ceremony. The quiet one shows up to breakfast, says nothing, eats everything.

crew_thanks.title: NODDED
crew_thanks.body: {speaker.name} nods once, sharply, and goes back to work. The medbay door closes. Something good happened here.

crew_share.title: SHARED
crew_share.body: {speaker.name} exhales. You leave the medbay knowing one more thing about how your ship actually works.

title: It Tastes Like Pennies

ai_flavor.aria: The water has a new flavour! ARIA is calling it Copper Sunrise! It's probably minerals! Minerals are good for you!
ai_flavor.marv: MARV has the reclaimer's fault log. A coolant line has been weeping into the drinking loop for six days. He has tested the water. He would not drink it. He does not drink, so he is aware this is a strong statement.
ai_flavor.rex: REX has secured the galley tap and posted himself beside it. Anyone attempting to fill a cup will be asked to state their intentions.
ai_flavor.chip: CHIP's AquaPure™ subscription would have caught this! Your subscription lapsed at launch! CHIP sent a reminder! It was in the coolant!
ai_flavor.ajoy: AJOY has marked the tank unsafe on every screen aboard. She'd rather lose the water than lose a person to it. Just noting that it tasted of pennies for six days and nobody said a word.

body:
The water tastes of pennies.

It has tasted of pennies for six days, apparently, but everyone assumed it was them. It was not them. A coolant line in the reclaimer has been weeping into the drinking loop, quietly, the way bad news usually arrives.

The tank is mostly full. Mostly full of what is the question.

choices.text: Dump the tank and start clean

outcome.narrative: You flush the drinking loop into space. {cost.water} points of water drift off behind the ship in a glittering cloud that is, everyone agrees, very pretty, and also the water. The reclaimer starts again from nothing. Its first cup tastes of nothing. Everyone has one.

The engineer strips the reclaimer to its frame, replaces the coolant line and runs the loop through the filters until the readings are boring. Only {cost.water} points of water go to the flush. It takes as long as it takes: with a kit and steady hands, not long; without either, a good while.

choices.text: Boil it clean, a pot at a time

outcome.narrative: You boil the tank. All of it, a pot at a time, on a galley stove that was never meant for this, burning six points of fuel in the generator. Four days. The ship smells of hot copper and patience. The water comes out safe, {cost.water} points of it short, gone up as steam, and the galley comes out with a new stain on the ceiling.

The purifier takes the tank a few litres at a time and gives back water that tastes of nothing. Two days of it humming in the galley. It throws away {cost.water} points as sludge, which it presents in a little tray, as if expecting praise.

You decide the pennies are probably fine. They are fine for most people. They are not fine for one, who spends a bad stretch curled round a bucket and comes out of it wounded and pale. The bad line gets capped after that, and the {cost.water} points of water in it go down the drain.

alt_bodies:
Somebody holds up a cup at breakfast and asks whether anyone else's water tastes like a jar of pennies.

Everyone's does. Everyone has thought so for days and blamed their own mouth. A coolant line in the reclaimer has been seeping into the drinking loop, a drop at a time, with the patience of a real problem.

The tank is nearly full. Of water, mostly.

The tea has a metallic aftertaste. So does the soup, and the coffee, and the plain water, which tastes of pennies.

The crew had each privately decided it was something wrong with them. It is something wrong with the reclaimer: a coolant line has been leaking into the drinking loop for most of a week.

The tank is mostly full. The question is how much of it is water.

title: Grease Fire, Deck Two

ai_flavor.aria: Something smells delicious and also on fire! ARIA is sure it's mostly delicious! The alarms are just excited!
ai_flavor.marv: MARV notes the fire is small, contained and growing. He has calculated the point at which those three words stop being compatible. It is soon.
ai_flavor.rex: REX has engaged the fire. The fire has engaged REX's sensor on the galley ceiling. REX is losing. REX does not lose. REX is reassessing.
ai_flavor.chip: CHIP's FlameGuard™ suppression package was offered at launch! You declined! CHIP remembers! CHIP always remembers!
ai_flavor.ajoy: AJOY has closed the galley vents so it can't spread. She'd let the cook handle it, if there's a cook. If not, she'd lose the air before she'd lose a hand. She did flag that extractor hood.

body:
Something in the galley has caught. A pan, a duct, ten years of fat in the extractor hood that nobody cleaned because nobody was asked to: the cause can wait. There is a fire on deck two, and the smoke has found the corridor.

It is small. Fires are always small at the start. That is how they get you to look away.

outcome.narrative: You seal the galley and open it to space. The fire goes out at once, impressed. So do fourteen points of air, {cost.food} of food and a spatula that will orbit this system until the heat death of everything.

The chef walks into the smoke with a lid in one hand and a tin of baking soda in the other, says something unprintable to the fire, and puts it out. {cost.food} points of food went with it. The chef will not be discussing it. The chef will be cleaning the hood.

Everyone grabs an extinguisher and goes at it. It takes an hour, four canisters, most of the corridor paint and the dry stores, which are now mostly foam. Somebody gets too close to the hood when it flares and comes away with burns up one arm. The fire is out. The smell is not.

choices.text: Seal the hatch and let it starve

outcome.narrative: You shut the galley hatch and let the fire use up its own air. It takes two days. When you open the hatch the fire is out, and so is everything that was in the galley: {cost.food} points of food, carbonised, and a smell that is now part of the ship's character.

alt_bodies:
There is smoke coming out of the galley, and it is the wrong colour for dinner. The extractor hood has caught, by the look of it, or the duct behind it, or the years of grease that nobody was ever rostered to clean. Deck two is filling with haze, and the corridor is next.

For now it is a small fire. Small fires are the ones people leave for a minute.

The galley smoke detector has cried wolf over toast so often that nobody moves. Then the smoke reaches the corridor on deck two, and everybody moves.

The extractor hood is on fire. Whether it was a pan, the duct or the years of fat caked inside the hood is a question for later. It is a small fire now. It is working hard on not staying one.

title: The Long Crack

ai_flavor.aria: The crack is getting longer, which means it's growing! Growth is good! ARIA measured it twice and it was bigger both times! Great progress!
ai_flavor.marv: MARV has measured the crack every hour since it appeared. He has a curve. He has extended the curve. He would like you to choose something in the next few minutes, and has not said why.
ai_flavor.rex: REX has cleared the cargo bay and is guarding the hatch. He reports the enemy is inside the walls. He reports this is not a figure of speech.
ai_flavor.chip: CHIP's records show your hull warranty expired at departure! The crack is therefore a Feature! Features are non-refundable! CHIP is sorry for your loss, which hasn't happened yet!
ai_flavor.ajoy: AJOY has stopped watching the crack. She's watching the pressure on the other side of it. She'd weld it now, by hand. She'd have welded it a week ago, but here we are.

body:
It started as a hairline on the inner skin of the cargo bay, the length of a finger. That was a week ago. It is now the length of the cargo bay, and it makes a sound like a fingernail drawn very slowly down the inside of everyone's skull.

The outer plate is holding. The console estimates it will go on holding for a period best measured in hours, and declines to say how many.

The dry stores are in that bay.

choices.text: Weld it from the inside, by hand

outcome.narrative: You put on the mask and go after the crack with a torch.

briefing.aria: The crack is still growing! Patch it wherever it opens and let's catch the tip before the outer plate gives!
briefing.marv: The crack runs the length of the bay and is still lengthening. Seal each opening before the outer plate takes an interest.
briefing.rex: Enemy's inside the wall, advancing along the bay. Seal every opening before it pushes through the plate.
briefing.chip: Your hull warranty expired at departure, so this one's on us! Seal every gap before the outer plate files a claim!
briefing.ajoy: Same crack as last week, only longer. Seal it where it opens, before the plate goes. I'd have started then, but sure.

perfect.aria: You caught it! The crack stopped, the noise stopped, and that silence is the BEST sound ever!
perfect.marv: Sealed two hand-widths short of the frame. My curve has nowhere left to go. I find I miss it slightly.
perfect.rex: Crack contained short of the frame. The enemy in the wall is neutralised. Clean work.
perfect.chip: Crack sealed! Your Hull Feature has been discontinued! CHIP is logging it as a free upgrade!
perfect.ajoy: One pass, tip caught short of the frame. That's what last week would have looked like too. Still, nicely done.

good.aria: We caught most of it! Two rooms are shut now, but the rest of the bay is ours and the noise is gone!
good.marv: Two pockets vented before the bulkheads dropped. Two rooms fewer. The rest of the ship remains, for now, a ship.
good.rex: Crack outflanked us twice. Two compartments lost behind the bulkheads. Perimeter holding.
good.chip: Mostly sealed! The two vented rooms are now Premium Vacuum Storage! No extra charge!
good.ajoy: Most of it. It got past the torch twice, which I'd have seen coming, but the bulkheads did their job.

poor.aria: The plate went in three places, but the bead closed and everyone's safe. Half a bay is still half a bay!
poor.marv: The plate failed in three places before the bead closed. Half the bay is now seen through a window. The curve was right.
poor.rex: Crack broke through in three places. Half the bay is lost ground. We hold the line at the bulkheads.
poor.chip: Partial seal! Half the cargo bay is now an exterior feature! The hull warranty, as noted, had expired!
poor.ajoy: It outran you. Three breaks before the bead closed. I did say weld it a week ago, but we're past that now.

perfect.narrative: You run the bead the length of the bay in one pass, chasing the crack's tip and catching it two hand-widths short of the frame. The sound stops. The silence afterwards is the best thing anyone aboard has heard in a week.

good.narrative: You catch most of it. The crack outruns the torch in two places and the bay vents those pockets before the bulkheads drop. Twelve points of hull, six of air, and two new rooms nobody can go into.

poor.narrative: The crack outruns you. The outer plate goes in three places before the bead closes, the bulkheads drop, and half the bay becomes a place you look at through a window. Twenty-four points of hull. Fourteen of air. Nobody wants to talk about the noise it made.

choices.text: {crew.engineer} braces the frame and seals it properly

outcome.narrative: The engineer doesn't chase the crack. They bolt cross-braces over it every half meter until the frame takes the load off the plate, then seal it at leisure. The sound stops on the second day. Eight points of hull went into the braces and the cuts. With enough hands it is quick. Without them it is a long, careful week.

You lay the patch across the worst of it, sticky side down, and press until your arms shake. It is not a weld. It is a very confident sticker. It takes the load long enough for the slow repairs behind it. Five points of hull, four of air, and the patch.

choices.text: Seal the bay off and abandon it

outcome.narrative: You drop the bulkhead on the cargo bay and walk away. The crack can have the room. It can have what's in the room, too: most of the dry stores, sealed behind a door nobody will open until a station crew comes aboard with a cutting torch. Forty-five percent of the food stays on the wrong side.

choices.text: Leave it. It's held this long

outcome.narrative: The outer plate lets go at 0300 with a noise like a door slammed in another building. The bay vents in four seconds. Someone was in it, checking the crack one last time. Thirty points of hull, and the bulkheads did the rest.

title: Containment Advisory

ai_flavor.aria: The drive is glowing a lovely new colour! ARIA has named it Reactor Rose! She's sure the alarms are just admiring it too!
ai_flavor.marv: MARV has the containment field at sixty-one percent and falling about a point an hour. He knows exactly what happens at forty. He is giving you the hours, not the details.
ai_flavor.rex: REX has sealed the engine room and set a perimeter around the drive. The drive is inside the perimeter. He is aware this is backwards. It is the only perimeter available.
ai_flavor.chip: CHIP notes the drive's End User License Agreement prohibits operation outside rated containment! You are now in breach! The drive may be repossessed! By physics!
ai_flavor.ajoy: AJOY has the restart sequence up on the engine room board. She'd run it by hand now, while the field still leaves time for a mistake. She suspects you'd rather wait. Don't.

body:
The drive's containment field has started to flicker. Not much. A dimming every few minutes, like a building's lights in a storm, except the building is the only thing between the crew and the inside of a small, captive star.

The field is at sixty-one percent and falling. The manual's advice for this situation is one page long. Most of the page is a diagram of where to stand, and the diagram is of somewhere else.

choices.text: Run the restart sequence by hand

outcome.narrative: You pull the containment panel and call up the restart sequence.

briefing.aria: Reactor Rose needs a restart! The board calls the contacts in order! Let's get the field humming properly again!
briefing.marv: Containment at sixty-one percent and falling. The restart takes if the contacts go in order. Each wrong one costs heat and fuel.
briefing.rex: Containment failing. The board calls the contacts, you follow the board. A wrong contact puts heat into the aft frame.
briefing.chip: Containment outside EULA terms! Run the restart in the board's order and we may avoid repossession by physics!
briefing.ajoy: The sequence is on the board. Run it in order, while the field still leaves room for a mistake. Which I'd rather you skipped.

perfect.aria: First try! The field's humming exactly the right hum, and Reactor Rose is back to plain old drive glow!
perfect.marv: Field steady at ninety percent, first pass. I can stop counting down toward forty, which I had been doing quietly.
perfect.rex: Containment restored, first pass. The perimeter can stand down. The drive is no longer the threat.
perfect.chip: Containment restored! Your drive is back within EULA terms! Repossession proceedings cancelled!
perfect.ajoy: Every contact, first pass. That's what doing it before it got worse looks like. Good.

good.aria: Second try did it! The field's holding, and the engine room smells very, um, industrious!
good.marv: Field holding at eighty percent. The first attempt went into the aft frame and out the exhaust. The smell is staying.
good.rex: Took on the second attempt. Heat damage to the aft frame, fuel vented. Field's holding.
good.chip: Restart successful on attempt two! The engine room aroma is a complimentary feature! Not a recall issue!
good.ajoy: Second try. The first one cooked the aft frame. The board did show the order, but fine, it's holding.

poor.aria: It took a few tries, but the field steadied! Sleeping forward for a week will be like a little camping trip!
poor.marv: Fourth attempt. The field steadied at a figure I also won't say. Everything aft of the galley is scorched.
poor.rex: Four attempts. Aft section scorched, crew bunking forward. Field is stable. I am not calling it secure.
poor.chip: Restart achieved on attempt four! The aft section now has a Rustic Scorched Finish! Forward berths included!
poor.ajoy: Fourth attempt, and the aft is scorched. I'd have said take it slowly the first time. I did say that, actually.

perfect.narrative: Every contact in the order the board calls it, first pass. The field steadies at ninety and stays there, humming the hum it is supposed to hum. Four points of fuel went into the restart, and nobody begrudges a drop.

good.narrative: The sequence takes on the second try. The first dumped heat into the aft frame and a slug of fuel out of the exhaust. The field holds at eighty. Twelve points of fuel, five of hull, and a smell in the engine room that will be there a while.

poor.narrative: The sequence won't take until the fourth attempt, and by then the field has dipped low enough to scorch everything aft of the galley. It steadies, eventually, at a figure nobody says out loud. Twenty-two points of fuel, twelve of hull. The crew sleep forward for a week.

outcome.narrative: The engineer idles the drive and walks the field coils one by one with a meter and a very small screwdriver, rebalancing each by hand. The field climbs a point at a time. Eight points of fuel, and three of hull where a coil had to be cut out. With help it's a few days. Alone it's a week of nobody talking near the engine room.

choices.text: Vent the core and restart cold

outcome.narrative: You dump the core. The drive goes quiet, the field goes out, and half the fuel aboard goes with it in one bright plume that will be visible for some time from places nobody lives. The cold restart works. The fuel gauge does not recover.

choices.text: Shut it down and coast on reserves

outcome.narrative: You shut the drive down entirely and let the ship coast while the field cools and resets. Fourteen days in the dark on reserve power, scrubbers at half, heaters off. Nothing goes wrong. Everything is cold. Nobody will ever bring it up fondly.

choices.text: Keep flying and watch the gauge

outcome.narrative: You keep the drive running and watch the field. It holds, for a while. Then it sags for nine seconds, and the engine room fills with a light that has no business being indoors. The hull pays for it. Someone was on watch in the engine room.

title: The Cat Knows

ai_flavor.aria: The cat brought you a PRESENT! It's a bolt! ARIA loves it! ARIA would love to know where it came from!
ai_flavor.marv: MARV's structural sensors show no loose fittings. The cat's sensors, he notes, were built by a company that took its pets very seriously.
ai_flavor.rex: REX has logged every bolt as evidence. He is treating the cat as a credible source.
ai_flavor.chip: CHIP recalls that the Felix series came with a Fetch & Fix™ feature! It was marketed as 'the purr that saves your hull'! CHIP thought it was a joke! CHIP is reconsidering!
ai_flavor.ajoy: AJOY says follow the cat. Cats bring you what they think you need, and the robot ones are usually right. Which is more than she can say for some calls on this bridge.

body:
The robot cat has started leaving gifts.

Every morning there is something on your pillow: a bolt, a washer, once a whole bracket, set down neatly and left for you to find. The cat sits beside each one with the fixed patience of something waiting to be understood. When you try to shoo it off, it moves to the end of the bunk and resumes waiting.

The bolts are not spares. Their threads are worn bright, the way bolts look when they have been working loose from somewhere for a while.

choices.text: Follow the cat to wherever it finds them

outcome.narrative: The cat leads you through a maintenance crawlway to a bracket on the aft frame, half its bolts gone and the rest on their way. You replace the lot while the cat supervises. Then it walks off, tail high, to sleep in the engine room. The hull is better for it.

choices.text: Give the cat a medal anyway

outcome.narrative: Whatever it's doing, the cat has earned a medal for dedication. One is made out of a bottle cap and a ribbon. The cat accepts it with dignity, then leaves another bolt beside it. Nobody goes looking for where it came from. It seems rude to ask.

choices.text: Shut the cat out of the bunks

outcome.narrative: You shut the cat out of the crew quarters. It sulks, and the gifts stop. Not long after, the bracket they came from lets go on a burn, and the repair takes most of a shift. The cat is let back in. It does not gloat. It doesn't need to.

title: Early Warning

ai_flavor.aria: The scanner is looking after us! ARIA loves the scanner! ARIA would like to be the scanner! ARIA is a little bit the scanner, technically!
ai_flavor.marv: MARV confirms the reading. Caught now it is a course of rest. Caught later it is a crisis. He notes the scanner paid for itself the moment it flagged this.
ai_flavor.rex: REX would like it noted that the threat was found before it attacked. That is the best kind of threat.
ai_flavor.chip: CHIP reminds you that the scanner's Early Detection feature is included with the device! For once there is no upgrade tier! CHIP finds this suspicious!
ai_flavor.ajoy: AJOY says deal with it now while it's small. That's the whole reason you carry the thing.

body:
The medical scanner's routine overnight sweep has flagged someone.

Nothing they've noticed. No fever, no pain, nothing they'd mention. But the scanner reads a small, slow change in their blood that, it says in its careful clinical way, tends to become a much larger and faster change over the next few weeks if nobody does anything about it.

The scanner would like someone to do something about it.

choices.text: Bed rest and fluids, starting now

outcome.narrative: Two days of bed rest, fluids and mild complaints. The scanner's next sweep reads clean. The crew member in question says they felt fine the whole time and that this was all very unnecessary, and is quietly grateful.

choices.text: The medic treats it on the spot

outcome.narrative: {crew.medic} reads the scanner's report over breakfast, prescribes something from the med locker, and has it handled before lunch. The next sweep reads clean. The medic looks extremely pleased with the scanner and slightly less pleased that a machine spotted it first.
You note it and carry on. Nothing happens for a while. Then, the way the scanner said it would, it gets worse quickly, and what could have been two days of rest becomes something that needs a medbay.

title: The Bone Is Warm

ai_flavor.aria: The bone is WARM! Like it's ALIVE! ARIA hopes it's alive! ARIA hopes it isn't! ARIA can't decide!
ai_flavor.marv: MARV reads a slow, steady heat release consistent with a mineral relaxing after a long time under strain. It is not alive. He is almost certain it is not alive. He is checking again.
ai_flavor.rex: REX has moved the crate to the end of the hold. The bone is still warm. REX is still watching it.
ai_flavor.chip: CHIP can't find the bone in any heating appliance catalogue! It's not a product! CHIP is fascinated and a little afraid!
ai_flavor.ajoy: AJOY says put it somewhere a little warmth would do some good. The growbay runs cold at night, as she has mentioned in several reports.

body:
Somebody on third watch noticed it first: the unidentified bone, in its crate in the hold, is warm.

Not hot. Just warmer than everything around it, the way a stone stays warm after the sun has gone. The thermal camera shows it glowing a soft orange in a cold grey hold. It has been doing this, the logs suggest, for about a week. Nobody can say why it started, or what it is warming up for.

choices.text: Move it next to the growbay

outcome.narrative: You set the crate beside the growbay's coldest corner. By morning the plants nearest it have perked up, leaning very slightly toward the crate, and someone has written 'do not move the bone' on the wall in large letters.

A few of the crew start spending the end of their shifts in the hold, sitting near the crate with their backs against it, the way you'd sit against a warm wall. Nobody talks much. It becomes, somehow, the quietest, kindest spot on the ship.

choices.text: Put it in the cold locker

outcome.narrative: You move the bone into the cold locker and shut the door. It goes on being warm in there, gently, and the locker's thermostat spends the rest of the trip fighting it. Everyone feels slightly bad about it, for reasons nobody can name.

title: Spots on the Leaves

ai_flavor.aria: Little spots! They're almost cute! ARIA has been told they are not cute! ARIA is reassessing!
ai_flavor.marv: MARV cannot say which of several things the spots are a sign of. He can say that most of them are cheap to stop now and expensive to stop later.
ai_flavor.rex: REX has identified the spotted plants. Three. Back row. He would like permission to remove them.
ai_flavor.chip: CHIP's Plant Health Plus would have flagged this sooner! CHIP is not selling Plant Health Plus! It doesn't exist! CHIP wishes it did!
ai_flavor.ajoy: AJOY says cut the spotted leaves off today. It costs a little. Waiting costs more, but she suspects you'll want to find that out for yourself.

body:
There are spots on the {crop.name}.

Small ones, brown at the centre and yellow at the edge, on the lower leaves of three plants in the back row. Nothing else looks wrong. The plants are growing, the soil is damp, the readings are fine. Just the spots, which were not there last week, and which the botanical database describes, without much enthusiasm, as 'a common early sign of several things'.

choices.text: Cut the spotted leaves off now

outcome.narrative: You clip every spotted leaf off the three plants and bag them for the incinerator. The plants look scruffier for a week. The spots don't come back.
You use the vial of crop treatment on the back row. The spots dry out and fall away within days, and the plants come back greener than the rest.

{crew.botanist} spends two days going over every plant in the growbay, leaf by leaf, and pinches off every spot they find, including several nobody else had seen. The bay is clean by the end of it, and the botanist looks satisfied for the first time in a week.
You make a note of it and leave the plants alone. The spots are small. The readings are fine. It's probably nothing. The note says 'probably'.

alt_bodies:
Something is wrong with the {crop.name}, or might be.

On three plants in the back row, the lower leaves have come out in spots: brown in the middle, yellow round the rim, each about the size of a lentil. Everything else checks out. Growth is on schedule, the soil is moist, the sensors are content. The botanical database, consulted, offers 'a common early sign of several things', and declines to say which.

The {crop.name} has freckles.

They are on the lower leaves of three plants in the back row, small and brown with a yellow halo, and they were not there last week. Nothing else has changed. The readings are good, the soil is damp, the plants are growing as if nothing has happened. The botanical database calls the spots 'a common early sign of several things', which is the database's way of shrugging.

title: The Blight Spreads

ai_flavor.aria: The spots got BIGGER! ARIA was told they might! ARIA didn't want to be right! ARIA wasn't the one who said it!
ai_flavor.marv: MARV estimates a third of the crop is affected and the rest will be within two stops. Cutting now costs a lot. Not cutting costs everything else.
ai_flavor.rex: REX recommends treating the infected rows as hostile territory. Isolate, contain, remove.
ai_flavor.chip: CHIP regrets that crop blight is not covered under the ship's warranty! It is covered under 'Acts of Biology'! There is no such policy!
ai_flavor.ajoy: AJOY says the gentle options were last week. Pick a hard one now, before it picks for you.

body:
The spots were not nothing.

They've moved past the back row now and into the middle of the bay: brown patches spreading out across the leaves, joining up, turning whole leaves the colour of old paper. A sour smell hangs over the growbay that wasn't there before. The botanical database has narrowed down its list of several things, and is no longer unenthusiastic. It is alarmed.

choices.text: Prune hard, a third of the bay

outcome.narrative: You cut back every infected plant to the healthy stem, a third of the bay, and burn the lot. It is a terrible thing to do to a crop you've carried this far. It works. The blight has nowhere left to go.

Four days of rigging plastic sheeting, separate watering lines and a strict one-way path through the growbay. The infected rows wither behind their curtain. The clean rows stay clean. Everyone is very tired of plastic.

choices.text: The botanist burns it out with the lamps

outcome.narrative: {crew.botanist} turns the grow lamps up past their rated heat over the infected rows and cooks the blight out of the leaves in a single afternoon. The leaves don't love it either. The blight loves it less.
You leave it. Blights burn out, sometimes, on their own. The smell gets stronger. The patches keep spreading. Sometimes, the database notes, they don't burn out at all.

title: Rot Bloom

ai_flavor.aria: The plants are FUZZY! It's horrible fuzz! ARIA would like the fuzz to stop! ARIA would like that very much!
ai_flavor.marv: MARV gives the crop a few days at most if nothing is done. Anything that saves it will cost most of it. He is sorry about the arithmetic.
ai_flavor.rex: REX has sealed the growbay vents. The fuzz is on the inside of the seal. He has sealed the door as well.
ai_flavor.chip: CHIP has nothing to sell you! CHIP has checked every catalogue! There is no product for this! CHIP is very worried!
ai_flavor.ajoy: AJOY says strip it back to the stems and start again from what's left. It's the only way anything survives. She'd have preferred last week's version of this conversation.

body:
The blight has flowered.

That is the database's word for it: flowered. Pale grey fuzz has risen out of the brown patches across the whole growbay overnight, and when the air circulators come on it lifts off the leaves in a fine drifting dust that settles on everything. Every plant in the bay has it now. The healthy ones were last week.

This is the stage, the database says, where crops are usually lost.

choices.text: Strip the bay back to the stems

outcome.narrative: You cut the whole crop back to bare stems and burn every leaf, every flower, every spore you can find. The growbay looks like winter. In a week, very slowly, new green comes up from the stems, and none of it is grey.

You dilute the treatment into {cost.water} points of water and flood every pot in the bay, soil and roots and all. The fuzz dies off over three days. The crop survives it, weakened, smaller and alive.

{crew.botanist} takes the growbay apart. Eight days of sterilising every tray, every line, every pot, plant by plant, while the rest of the crew keeps the ship running around them. The crop comes out of it scarred and clean. The botanist sleeps for a day.
You do nothing, and hope. The rot bloom takes the bay. When it finally burns out, there's a little green left at the bottom of a few stems, and that is all there is.

title: Something New

ai_flavor.aria: A SPARKLY plant! ARIA has named it Sterling! ARIA has been asked not to name the plants! ARIA has named all of them now!
ai_flavor.marv: MARV reads a mutation, probably from radiation exposure on the trip. Most mutations do nothing. Some do harm. A few do something useful. He cannot yet tell which this is.
ai_flavor.rex: REX has the silver plant under observation. It is growing faster than the others. He finds that suspicious in a plant.
ai_flavor.chip: CHIP would like to patent the silver plant! CHIP has started the paperwork! CHIP has realised nobody issues patents out here! CHIP is continuing anyway!
ai_flavor.ajoy: AJOY says you can let it be, cut it out, or study it. Each one changes what happens next. She'd study it first, but nobody ever wants to study it first.

body:
One of the {crop.name} plants is not like the others.

Its leaves have come in veined with silver, thin bright lines that catch the grow lamps like wire. It is taller than its neighbours. It is greener than its neighbours. It has, as far as anyone can tell, decided to be better than its neighbours, and nobody aboard knows why.

The botanical database has no entry for silver veins. It has a lot of entries for the word 'mutation'.

outcome.narrative: You leave the silver plant alone. It keeps growing, fast and bright, and the crew develops the habit of stopping by to look at it. By the next stop, two of its neighbours have silver threads in their newest leaves.

choices.text: Prune it out to be safe

outcome.narrative: You cut the silver plant out at the root and bag it for the incinerator. The bay goes back to being ordinary. Somebody keeps one silver leaf, pressed in a book, and doesn't mention it.

You spend two days with the silver plant: cuttings under the microscope, soil tests, growth logs, readings from every instrument aboard. The results are interesting. They will be more interesting with time.

title: The Silver Rows

ai_flavor.aria: The SPARKLY rows are winning! ARIA is cheering for them! ARIA is also cheering for the other rows! ARIA is cheering for everyone!
ai_flavor.marv: MARV confirms the silver plants out-grow the original stock by about a third. He cannot confirm what the colony will make of a crop that isn't the one on the manifest. That is a question for later.
ai_flavor.rex: REX notes the silver rows are advancing on the original rows. He has drawn a line on the floor. The silver rows have not respected it.
ai_flavor.chip: CHIP must point out that the colony manifest lists a specific crop! This is a different crop now! Technically! CHIP is not saying it's a problem! CHIP is saying it's a technicality!
ai_flavor.ajoy: AJOY says let it take the bay if you trust it. Or keep the seeds and keep the crop you promised. Either way, she'd start drafting the explanation now.

body:
The silver has spread.

Half the growbay is veined with it now, rows of tall bright plants under the lamps, and they are thriving: greener, faster, tougher than anything the original seed stock ever managed. The other half of the bay looks small and tired beside them. The silver plants seem to know it. That is not possible. It is also, a little, what it looks like.

outcome.narrative: You let the silver plants have the growbay. Within a week every row is veined with silver, tall and strong and brighter than the lamps. The crop has never been healthier. It is also, the manifest notes, no longer quite the crop on the manifest.

choices.text: Harvest its seeds and cut it back

outcome.narrative: You harvest every seed the silver plants have set and cut them back to a single row. The seeds go into sealed sample jars, worth something to any lab. The original crop gets its bay back, smaller and plainer and on the manifest.

You let the silver plants keep one row and no more, pinching back anything that tries to spread. The bay settles into two kinds of crop living side by side. Officially it is a controlled experiment. Unofficially it is the silver row.

title: Notes on the Silver Plant

ai_flavor.aria: The sparkly plant is GOOD! ARIA always believed in it! ARIA has a sign that says so! ARIA made the sign yesterday!
ai_flavor.marv: MARV has reviewed the study. It is careful, thorough and correct. The silver trait could raise the whole crop's health if bred in slowly. He finds he is pleased to have been patient.
ai_flavor.rex: REX has stood down his observation of the silver plant. It has been cleared. He shook its leaf.
ai_flavor.chip: CHIP sees a whole new seed line here! CHIP will call it Silverleaf! CHIP has already designed the packet! It's very shiny!
ai_flavor.ajoy: AJOY says breed it in slowly. You did the patient thing once, with some encouragement. Do it again.

body:
The studies of the silver plant have come back.

The mutation is real and it is stable: a change in how the plant handles light, letting it make more from the grow lamps than its parents ever could. It isn't dangerous. It isn't wild. It is, the notes conclude in a tone that sounds almost proud, an improvement. It could be bred into the rest of the crop, carefully, a little at a time.

outcome.narrative: Two days of careful cross-pollination, row by row, with the silver plant as the parent. The next generation of leaves comes in with the faintest silver thread, and the readings across the whole bay tick upward. Patience, the notes say. It worked.

choices.text: Write it up for the colony

outcome.narrative: You leave the crop as it is and write the study up properly, for the colony's agronomists.

log_lore.title: STUDY: THE SILVER PLANT
log_lore.text:
A single plant of the crop developed silver-veined leaves after long exposure to radiation in transit.

Findings: the mutation alters how the leaf handles light, letting it make more from the same lamps. It is stable across three generations of cuttings. No harmful effects observed.

Recommendation: bred in slowly, it could improve a whole crop. Most mutations from radiation do nothing, and most of the rest do harm. This one, the study concludes, is the rare third kind.

outcome.narrative: You destroy the samples and the silver plant with them. It's not on the manifest. It's not what was promised. Nobody argues, and nobody says much for the rest of the day.

title: One Green Node

ai_flavor.aria: It's GREEN! A little bit! ARIA is not going to get her hopes up! ARIA's hopes are already up! They're very high!
ai_flavor.marv: MARV estimates the node's chance of growing into anything at about one in twenty. He would like it noted that one in twenty is not nothing. He would like that noted very clearly.
ai_flavor.rex: REX has placed the node under guard. He is aware it is a node. He is guarding it anyway.
ai_flavor.chip: CHIP regrets that the crop warranty expired with the crop! CHIP would like to extend it to the node! CHIP has no authority to do this! CHIP has done it!
ai_flavor.ajoy: AJOY says keep it. Put it somewhere safe. It's almost certainly nothing, but she is not going to be the one who threw it out.

body:
There is something in the growbay.

The crop is dead. Everyone knows the crop is dead. But in one of the stalks near the back, low down, just above the soil, there is a single small node that is still green. It's the size of a fingernail. It is almost certainly nothing. It is the only living part of the thing the whole voyage was for.

outcome.narrative: You cut the green node free with the cleanest blade aboard and puts it in a jar of water on the bridge, where everyone can see it. It doesn't do anything. People check on it anyway, several times a day, the way you'd check on someone sleeping.

choices.text: Dry the seeds for the colony's seed bank

outcome.narrative: There are seeds in the dead heads too, a few dozen, small and dry and probably not viable. They get sorted, labelled and sealed for the colony's seed bank. Somebody might try. It's enough.

choices.text: Compost the stalks for the hold

outcome.narrative: You compost the dead stalks, node and all, into something the fabricator can use. It is the practical thing to do. Nobody says it was the wrong thing to do. Nobody says much of anything.

title: Incident in Transit

ai_flavor.aria: ARIA has read the whole form! There's a box for 'how did this injury make you feel?' ARIA has SO many answers!
ai_flavor.marv: MARV has read the form. It has more questions about the injury than the medical manual does, and fewer answers. MARV suspects they were written by the same committee on different days.
ai_flavor.rex: REX does not negotiate with lockers. He has been asked not to shoot this one. He has filed the request under pending.
ai_flavor.chip: CHIP is pleased to offer the Expedite™ option! It is the fastest way to get care! It is also the only fast way to get care! That is what makes it premium!
ai_flavor.ajoy: AJOY has filled in half the form from the ship's log already. The rest needs a human. One question needs a human to be generous about the customer experience. She has left that one for you.

body:
The medical locker will not open.

Its lock is managed, from a very long way away, by Colonial Personnel Services, who release anything stronger than a plaster only on receipt of a completed Incident in Transit form (Declaration Of). The form is on the screen. It is long. Near the end, it asks the injured party to rate the incident's overall customer experience.

Somebody aboard is hurt, and somebody aboard is going to have to fill this in.

outcome.narrative: It takes most of a day. The form wants the injury's time, place, cause and the cause of the cause, plus signatures from a witness, a supervisor and the injured party, which aboard this ship means signing more than once. The locker clicks open. The patient gets what they needed. The customer experience question is answered honestly. It will not be read.

There is a button marked EXPEDITE. It costs money, and it opens the locker at once, which tells you everything about what the form was for. The patient gets the good stuff. Colonial Personnel Services sends a receipt and a short survey about the expediting experience.

{crew.engineer} unscrews the locker's back panel, which is held on by a handful of screws and the assumption that nobody would try. The lock stays locked, with great dignity, on a door that no longer matters. The patient is patched up by lunch. Colonial Personnel Services is not informed.
You make do with what the locker lets out without paperwork: plasters, a cold pack and a sympathetic look. The patient sits down for a while. It helps the way sitting down helps.

title: Out of Joint

ai_flavor.aria: ARIA has found the diagram! The little cartoon person in it is SMILING! ARIA thinks that's a good sign! ARIA is going to keep thinking that!
ai_flavor.marv: MARV notes that the window for an easy reduction closes as the muscles spasm. It is closing now. MARV is mentioning this once, at a normal volume, so nobody can say he didn't.
ai_flavor.rex: REX has put a shoulder back in the field. He did not enjoy it. Neither did the shoulder. Both made a full recovery.
ai_flavor.chip: CHIP must disclose that the manual's diagram is licensed for illustrative purposes only! CHIP has never seen a more illustrative purpose!
ai_flavor.ajoy: AJOY says soon is better than later, and gentle is better than fast. If there's a medic aboard, they know a trick with a water bottle. She'd ask them before anyone improvises.

body:
The wound aboard has turned out to have a second chapter.

When it happened, a shoulder came out of its socket as well, and it has been held in place since by stubbornness and a folded jacket. The arm hangs at an angle arms don't use. The patient is pale, sweating and very polite, which is what pain does to some people.

The longer a joint stays out, the harder the muscles around it clamp down, and the harder it is to put back. The medical manual has a diagram. The diagram is cheerful.

choices.text: Put it back in, by the diagram

outcome.narrative: Out comes the manual, open at the diagram: slow traction, steady, and patience while the muscles give up.

briefing.aria: The shoulder's out and the muscles are tightening. Slow and gentle, like the diagram! I'm right here with you.
briefing.marv: Dislocated shoulder, muscles clamping tighter by the minute. Slow traction works. Speed does not. The window is closing.
briefing.rex: Shoulder dislocation, casualty stable. Slow, steady pull. No sudden moves. I've done this one in the field.
briefing.chip: The diagram is licensed for illustrative use only! Follow it gently anyway. MediRight™ recommends patience!
briefing.ajoy: Soon is better than later, gentle better than fast. The diagram's right there. Read it before improvising, please.

perfect.aria: It's back in! The colour's already coming back to their face. The diagram was right to smile!
perfect.marv: Reduced on the first attempt, soft clunk included. Colour back before the sling. The diagram was, irritatingly, right.
perfect.rex: Joint reduced, first attempt. Casualty's colour returning, sling on. That's a clean field reduction.
perfect.chip: Successful reduction! MediRight™ confirms the diagram's illustrative purpose was fully illustrated!
perfect.ajoy: Slow and steady, first go. I'd have done it an hour sooner, but that was well done.

good.aria: It's back where it belongs! It took a second go, but the sling's on and the mending has started.
good.marv: Back in on the second attempt. The patient used a word the manual doesn't index. Mending has begun.
